prompt: What does the scaling factor on line 2 of POSCAR do?

options.text: It multiplies every lattice vector (and Cartesian positions)
options.why: A value of 5.43 turns the unit vectors written below into angstrom lengths.

options.text: It sets the number of atoms
options.why: Tempting because it is a number near the top, but the counts are on line 7.
Tempting, but the cutoff is ENCUT in INCAR.

hints: Look at what the lattice-vector lines are multiplied by.
A negative value would be a volume.

prompt: The species line of POSCAR says "Ti O". In which order must POTCAR be built?

options.why: POTCAR is the element files joined in the same order as the species line.
Tempting if you sort alphabetically, but VASP pairs potentials with species by position.
Tempting, but VASP matches by order, so the wrong order gives atoms the wrong potentials.

hints: VASP pairs the n-th species with the n-th dataset.
Check with grep TITEL POTCAR.

prompt: A POSCAR written in fractions of the lattice vectors is read as Cartesian by mistake. What happens?

options.text: The fractions are read as angstrom, so atoms pile up close to each other
options.why: Values like 0.25 become 0.25 angstrom; VASP warns that some ions are very close.
Tempting, but VASP follows the Direct or Cartesian line literally.
Tempting, but the lattice is read the same way; it is the positions that are misread.

hints: What does 0.25 mean in each mode?
Look at the error about distances between ions.

prompt: What does "F F F" after an atom mean under Selective dynamics?

options.text: That atom stays fixed in x, y and z during relaxation
options.why: F means the coordinate may not move; T means it may.

options.text: The atom is a fluorine atom
options.why: Tempting, but species come from the species line, not from flags.

options.text: The atom carries no magnetic moment
options.why: Tempting, but moments are set by MAGMOM in INCAR.

hints: T and F are true and false.
Used to freeze the bottom layers of a slab.

prompt: A primitive fcc cell has scaling factor 4.0 angstrom and lattice vectors (0, 0.5, 0.5), (0.5, 0, 0.5), (0.5, 0.5, 0). What is its volume in cubic angstrom?
hints: The determinant of the three vectors is 1/4.
V = s^3 times the determinant.

prompt: Which mesh type is required for hexagonal cells?

options.why: Shifted meshes can break hexagonal symmetry; Gamma-centred meshes are required.
Tempting because it is efficient for cubic cells, but it shifts the mesh off Gamma and breaks hexagonal symmetry.
Tempting, but line mode is for band paths, not for sampling the zone.

hints: Which mesh always contains the zone centre?
The Field Handbook calls it a safe default for any lattice.

prompt: A cell is made twice as long along a. How should the subdivisions along b1 change?

options.why: N_i times a_i stays roughly constant: a longer cell has a shorter reciprocal vector.
Tempting because the cell is bigger, but the reciprocal vector is shorter, so fewer points are needed.
Tempting, but that oversamples the zone and wastes time.

hints: Real and reciprocal lengths are inverse.
Think of a supercell.

prompt: Why should a band-structure line path not be used in a self-consistent run?

options.text: Its points do not sample the Brillouin zone evenly, so the density would be wrong
options.why: The SCF needs a uniform mesh; the path is for eigenvalues only.
Tempting, but VASP reads line mode for non-self-consistent band runs.

options.text: A path has too many k-points
options.why: Tempting, but the problem is uneven sampling, not the count.

hints: What does the SCF average over?
Bands come from ICHARG = 11 or KPOINTS_OPT.

prompt: Which statements about KPOINTS are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: Without a KPOINTS file VASP can build a mesh from KSPACING
options.why: KSPACING in INCAR replaces the file.

options.text: The 0 on line 2 means generate the mesh automatically
options.why: That is the automatic mode.

options.text: Metals usually need denser meshes than insulators
options.why: The Fermi surface must be resolved.
Tempting, but it is optional; 0 0 0 is the usual value.

hints: Read the five lines of the example again.
Metals have bands crossing the Fermi level.

prompt: What happens to an INCAR tag you leave out?

options.text: VASP uses its default, which may depend on other tags
options.why: For example IBRION defaults to -1 when NSW = 0.
Tempting, but most tags are optional.
Tempting, but VASP runs in batch and never asks.

hints: Most of INCAR is optional.
Defaults can depend on each other.

prompt: You typed ENCUTT = 520. How do you find out what cutoff VASP actually used?

options.text: Look at the parameter echo near the top of OUTCAR (grep ENCUT OUTCAR)
options.why: VASP prints every parameter it used; a misspelled tag may have been ignored.

options.text: VASP always stops on a typo
options.why: Tempting, but a misspelled tag may be ignored silently.
Tempting because it is short, but it lists energies, not parameters.

hints: Which file lists the parameters?
A typo may be ignored.

prompt: EDIFFG = -0.005. When does the relaxation stop?

options.text: When every force is below 0.005 eV per angstrom
options.why: A negative EDIFFG is a force criterion.

options.text: When the energy changes by less than 0.005 eV
options.why: Tempting, but that is the meaning of a positive EDIFFG.
Tempting as a joke, but EDIFFG is an accuracy criterion.

hints: The sign matters.
Negative means forces.

prompt: Which of these are valid INCAR syntax? Select all that apply.

options.why: ! starts a comment.
; separates two tags on one line.
# also starts a comment.
Tempting from other formats, but INCAR uses =.

hints: TAG = value.
Two comment characters are allowed.

prompt: Why should you set ENCUT, EDIFF, ISMEAR and spin yourself even when VASPKIT wrote the INCAR?

options.text: The templates start from conservative defaults that were not chosen for your system
options.why: The LR template even leaves ENCUT commented out.

options.text: VASPKIT INCARs cannot be read by VASP
options.why: Tempting, but they are ordinary INCARs.
Tempting, but they do; the defaults are just not right for every system.

hints: A template was written for no system in particular.
The Workflow Handbook says so explicitly.

prompt: Which POTCAR line tells you the recommended minimum cutoff?

options.why: grep ENMAX POTCAR; take the largest over all species.
Tempting, but ZVAL is the number of valence electrons.
Tempting, but TITEL names the dataset.

hints: Look for the word MAX.
The protocol multiplies it by 1.3.

prompt: What does the _pv suffix in Ti_pv mean?

options.text: Semicore p states are treated as valence
options.why: More electrons, more accurate, more expensive.
Tempting, but all PAW datasets are used with plane waves.

options.text: A dataset for PBE only with van der Waals
options.why: Tempting, but van der Waals corrections are INCAR tags, not POTCAR variants.

hints: p and v.
Compare _sv.

prompt: A colleague asks you to post your POTCAR in a public forum. What should you do?

options.text: Share the TITEL lines instead; POTCAR files are licensed and must not be redistributed
options.why: The TITEL list identifies the datasets without sharing their content.

options.text: Post it; it is just text
options.why: Tempting, but POTCAR files are licensed by VASP Software GmbH.
Tempting, but part of the file is still licensed content.

hints: Who owns the POTCAR library?
What identifies a dataset without its content?

prompt: POTCAR lists ENMAX values of 400.0 and 282.9 eV. What ENCUT does the protocol use for the relaxation?
hints: Take the largest ENMAX.
Multiply it by 1.3.

prompt: Which file do you copy to POSCAR to continue from the latest structure?

options.why: It holds the latest structure in POSCAR format.
Tempting because it has structures, but it is the trajectory of every step.
Tempting, but it is a log, not an input file.

hints: CONT for continue.
Same format as POSCAR.

prompt: Which file does a run with ICHARG = 11 read?

options.why: It holds the self-consistent density that the non-self-consistent run keeps fixed.
Tempting because it is also a density, but CHG is lower precision and cannot restart a run.
Tempting, but WAVECAR is the wavefunctions, read with ISTART.

hints: ICHARG is about the charge.
Which density file is high precision?

prompt: IBZKPT lists far more k-points than you expected. What is the likely cause?

options.text: VASP found lower symmetry than you intended, for example because MAGMOM breaks it
options.why: Fewer symmetry operations leave more irreducible points.
Tempting, but IBZKPT is built from your mesh.
Tempting, but the cutoff does not change the k-points.

hints: IBZKPT is reduced by symmetry.
What can lower symmetry?

prompt: What does CHGCAR store on its grid?

options.text: The density times the cell volume
options.why: Divide by the volume to get electrons per cubic angstrom.

options.text: The density in electrons per cubic angstrom
options.why: Tempting, but the stored values are multiplied by the cell volume.
Tempting, but those are in WAVECAR.

hints: The Field Handbook gives the unit.
The average of the values is the number of electrons.

prompt: Which tags make VASP write which file? Select all correct pairs.

options.text: LORBIT = 11 writes PROCAR and the projected DOS
options.why: Projections need LORBIT 10 or more.
Used for Bader analysis.
Tempting, but .FALSE. means it is not written.
The local potential, for work functions.

hints: Each special file needs its own tag.
.FALSE. turns writing off.
